A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiscoSG research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original scene-graph parsing, downstream evaluation, ablation, lexical-diversity, and human-error-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional split-based evaluations, comparator results, and active-learning validation scores.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same sentence-merging Generator, encoder-based deletion classifier, decoder-based insertion generator, deterministic Interpreter, synthetic edit construction, and joint training losses. The added GraphRAG procedure is a comparator, not a proposed-method change.

E1.justification: The dataset and task coverage remains unchanged, including DiscoSG-DS, DetailCaps, CapArena, and D-FOIL. Random and Length partition the existing annotated corpus differently; this changes evaluation design within retained coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GraphRAG-GPT-4o and an expert-only DiscoSG-T5-large (300) comparator to parsing evaluation. Its downstream table also adds DiscoSG-T5-base and DiscoSG-T5-large under SPICE, BSSPICE, and CAPTURE. The existing comparison families and methods remain.

E3.justification: The single 300/100 train/test partition becomes two partitions: uniform Random and Length, which trains on fewer-triple graphs and tests on more complex graphs. This substantially extends the evaluation design to complexity generalization. v2 also adds a 300-example T5-large control and an entity/relation-conditioned GraphRAG prompting protocol.

E4.justification: The new Length evaluation systematically tests generalization from simpler to more complex graphs, an important robustness question absent from v1. v2 also reports active-learning validation progression and adds a training-size control. The existing component ablations, lexical-diversity analysis, and appendix case study are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The 50-sample human/GPT agreement assessment and its Jaccard/F1 measures are retained; changed agreement values are results changes. The additional split is not reported as repeated-run uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v1 Table 2 versus v2 Table 3 substantially revises baseline scores: DiscoSG-T5-base reports 30.0 versus 52.7 SPICE, and T5-xl 61.1 versus 76.8 in the corresponding Random column. Refiner-xl remains 66.7, reversing its ranking against T5-xl. These are reported revisions, not established same-setting performance improvements. v2 adds Length and comparator results, revises downstream average ranks, and changes Appendix A.3 agreement from 65.7/69.7 to 70.9/74.4 Jaccard/F1.

T1.justification: The graph definitions, probabilistic formulation, edit operations, loss formulation, active-learning algorithm, and SPICE/BSSPICE mathematics are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation appears.

C1.justification: The principal task, dataset, refinement-framework, and D-FOIL contributions remain. The abstract newly emphasizes robustness to complex graph generation, while the introduction replaces approximately 15 times more objects/relations with at least three times more triples. The central approximately 30% advantage over sentence merging remains.

C2.justification: The central performance interpretation shifts substantially. v1 emphasizes broadly poor direct fine-tuning and refinement outperforming all nonteacher baselines; v2 recognizes strong T5 performance on Random and locates refinement's advantage in generalization to complex Length graphs. It also interprets new downstream T5 comparisons as architectural evidence and acknowledges potential internal-annotator bias. The text-only limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds GraphRAG prompting details, MTurk-sandbox and annotator recruitment/payment disclosures, and proposed dataset-release terms. Appendix B.5 leaves the license choice as '[MIT/Apache 2.0/CC BY 4.0]', so no specific license is established. Existing Programmer training settings, hardware information, and code/data URL remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Edge et al.'s GraphRAG work and positions an evaluated variant among prompting comparators. The related-work discussion otherwise remains substantively stable. CapArena's updated publication information identifies the same cited work.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract, introduction, experimental discussion, and conclusion, expands affiliations, and adds acknowledgments and author contributions. Lexical diversity moves from Appendix B.4 to C, and prompts move from C to D. The main section sequence and method exposition remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: A new first-page Table 1 condenses the retained appendix Figure 1 example. The parsing table becomes full-width with Random/Length columns, the downstream table gains comparator rows, and Algorithm 1 receives larger typesetting. Existing case-study and prompt figures remain.

improvement.justification: The complexity-generalization test and downstream fine-tuning controls make v2's comparative evidence more informative, and Section 4.1 better qualifies the refinement advantage. Appendix Table 7 also fixes human-error entries that previously disagreed with column averages. These gains improve clarity and internal consistency, although large baseline-score revisions remain unexplained and Appendix B.5 contains an unresolved license placeholder.
